description.p: OneKeePass keeps your passwords and other sensitive information in a single encrypted KeePass-compatible database file (KDBX 4). The file stays yours: keep it on your computer, on a USB drive, or on cloud storage you already use.

Everything happens on your own machine. There is no account to create, no server to trust and no telemetry. Databases are encrypted with AES-256 or ChaCha20 and unlocked with a master password, a key file, or both.

ul.li: Entries organised by type, category, tag or the standard group tree
Custom entry types and any number of custom fields, grouped into sections
Built-in entry types for SSH keys, identities, passports and driver licences
Time-based one-time passwords (TOTP) with a live countdown
File attachments, and custom icons for entries and groups
Open databases directly over SFTP or WebDAV, without a third-party sync tool
Import CSV exports from Bitwarden, 1Password, LastPass and others
Merge databases, clone entries, and work with several databases at once

description.p: Application data now follows the XDG layout and is kept in the application's own data directory.
Access to the system keyring is no longer requested. The encryption key held for an open database stays within the running application instead.
The first release published on Flathub. The Flatpak is built entirely from source, the user interface included, so what is shipped can be checked against what is published.

Checking for updates now explains that your package manager provides them instead of offering a download, and the recent databases list shows plain file names for databases opened through the desktop file chooser.
Locking a database now removes its decrypted content from memory, and databases lock automatically when the computer sleeps.

CSV import recognises the export files of many password managers, the password generator gained an exclude-similar-characters option and colour coded output, and an optional auto-save-after-edit setting was added.
